description: The only way to give this round's answer when it is a plan. Fill the fields and call it; the platform builds and stores the answer from them. Do not write the answer as text.

parameters.plan: The plan, with the fields below.
parameters.plan.stages: array of {stageId, title, description?}. A task references a stage only through its own stageId.
parameters.plan.tasks: array of {taskId, stageId?, title, requirementLevel, taskKind, disposition, scope, executionIntent?}. requirementLevel is "required" or "optional". taskKind is "work" or "gate". disposition is "active", "deferred", "cancelled" or "superseded". Every task of a NEW plan starts "pending". scope is {kind:"goal"}, {kind:"stage",stageId} or {kind:"module",stageId,moduleRef}. Task scope.moduleRef is a non-empty STRING containing the moduleId, NOT the {projectId,moduleId} object used in the architecture catalog. executionIntent is "plan_only" or "request_execution" and may appear on a work task only.
parameters.plan.assignments: array of {taskId, role, instruction}. A work task with executionIntent "request_execution" needs exactly one assignment whose role is one of the AVAILABLE roles/templateId shown in this context; a work task with executionIntent "plan_only" may omit it; a gate task must never carry an assignment or an executionIntent, because a gate conclusion comes from the formal evidence reduction, not from an execution run. A future work task with executionIntent "plan_only" may omit assignment, obligations/acceptance and dependencies; its incompleteness alone is not a reason to answer with questions instead.
parameters.plan.obligations: array of {obligationId, title, requirementLevel, taskIds, verificationRequirements}. taskIds lists only work/gate tasks of this same plan. Every verificationRequirements entry is {requirementId, requirementLevel, kind, description}; requirementLevel is "required" or "optional" and kind must be one of the requirementKinds of the effective CompletionPolicy shown in this context. A required obligation needs at least the policy's minimum number of required verification requirements.
parameters.plan.taskHierarchy: {parentOf:[{parentTaskId, childTaskId}]}. It only expresses display grouping.
parameters.plan.executionDag: {dependsOn:[{taskId, dependsOnId, requires:{kind, label}}]}. requires.kind is "output-contract", "artifact", "decision", "environment-revision" or "gate-result"; use a real versioned input/output dependency, keep the DAG acyclic and never make a task depend on itself.
parameters.plan.taskRelations: Optional: array of {fromTaskId, toTaskId, kind, note}; kind is "coordination" or "expected_dependency". It is advisory only and never a dispatch prerequisite.
parameters.setup: Required in this round: this project has no adopted architecture or no active completion policy yet. It has exactly these three fields: architecture, completionPolicy and checks. The OPTIONAL and "Omit setup" wording does not apply.
parameters.setup.architecture: architecture: {baselineId, description, constraints:[{name, scope}], catalog:{dependencies:[{from, to, reason}], modules:[{moduleId, name, responsibility, paths, interfaces:[{id, description, paths}]}], containment?}}. Name every module by its bare moduleId; the platform fills the projectId of every module ref, dependency and containment pair. containment is OPTIONAL: give a parent/child pair only when the real sources show that one module contains the other; omit containment when you do not know (an omitted containment means unknown, never flat); an explicit {parentOf:[]} means every module is flat; never derive a parent from paths or dependencies.
parameters.setup.completionPolicy: completionPolicy: {requirementKinds:[...], minimumRequiredRequirementsPerObligation:N}. Copy the requirementKinds of the effective CompletionPolicy shown in this context. When no policy is shown, propose the smallest REAL policy this request needs; never emit an empty policy whose vacuously satisfied obligations would auto-PASS.
parameters.setup.checks: array of {checkId, kind, command, cwd, timeoutMs, taskIds}. "kind" is exactly a policy requirement kind ("static" or "dynamic") and maps directly to the requirement.kind it satisfies; there is NO coverage field and never add one. taskIds is "all" or the real task ids. Use only a command that must really run for this request: never assume a test file exists, never copy an unrelated command, and never invent an empty check list to force a PASS.
parameters.goalCardDrafts: Only when this request has no goal: at least one draft. Each draft is {objective, completion, autonomy, screening}: objective one sentence; completion a non-empty array of checkable completion criteria; autonomy "every_step" or "after_plan_confirmation"; screening is optional: omit it or use null when you did not screen the draft, otherwise {modules, size, conflictsWith, dependsOn, urgency, suggestedPosition, note} with bare moduleIds and goalIds for the platform to fill their refs; size is "small", "medium", "large" or "unknown", urgency is "high", "normal" or "low", suggestedPosition is null or an integer >= 0, note is at most 512 UTF-8 bytes. A draft is a proposal only.
parameters.planDraftIndex: Only when this request has no goal: the zero-based index of the goalCardDrafts entry this plan is for.
